title: College Essay Human Voice Alibi Studio
oneLiner: A playful admissions-anxiety studio that helps applicants prove their essay sounds human without turning their story into AI-detector paranoia.
targetUser: Anxious college applicants, parents, counselors, and high-school writers worried that AI scoring or AI detectors will misread a real essay.
keyUx: Paste drafts, add personal memory fragments, process notes, counselor comments, and version history; visualize over-polish risk, collect human-proof artifacts, rehearse authenticity answers, and create a shareable voice receipt.
inspiredBySignals: Signal 9 — Los Angeles Times — AI may be scoring college admissions essays: https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-01-02/ai-may-be-scoring-your-college-admissions-essay
Signal 10 — Reddit r/CollegeAdmissions — parents debating AI detectors and false positives: https://www.reddit.com/r/CollegeAdmissions/comments/1s3yjdy/for_parents_of_kids_who_are_starting_their/
stitchPrompt: Design a playful experimental education product called College Essay Human Voice Alibi Studio for anxious college applicants, parents, counselors, and high-school writers worried that AI scoring or AI detectors will misread a real essay. Users should paste essay drafts, add personal memory fragments, writing-process notes, counselor comments, and version history, then visualize whether the essay sounds over-polished, collect human-proof artifacts, rehearse authenticity answers, and create a funny-but-useful voice receipt. Include a draft paste lane, human memory ingredient wall, over-polish heatmap, version-history scrapbook, authenticity interview rehearsal cards, parent panic meter, and shareable human-voice receipt. Design direction: use a playful-experimental aesthetic with scrapbook textures, bold school-notebook accents, animated detector ghosts, high-contrast before/after voice cards, and cheeky but supportive microcopy so the product feels portfolio-worthy and emotionally sharp rather than a sterile plagiarism checker.
